questions.question: Draw up a three-column table comparing a plant cell and an animal cell for: cell wall, vacuole, chloroplasts, shape and position of the nucleus.
questions.expected_answer: Cell wall: plant has a cellulose cell wall; animal has none. Vacuole: plant has one large permanent vacuole with cell sap; animal has small temporary vacuoles or none. Chloroplasts: plant has them in green parts; animal has none. Shape: plant regular and box-like; animal irregular and rounded. Nucleus: plant at the edge, pushed by the vacuole; animal near the centre.

questions.question: A learner claims that the cell wall controls what enters a plant cell. Correct the claim and explain the relationship between the wall and the membrane.
questions.expected_answer: The cell wall is fully permeable and does not control entry; it gives support, shape and protection. The cell membrane, which lies just inside the wall, is selectively permeable and controls which substances enter and leave. A plant cell has both structures, the wall outside and the membrane inside.

questions.question: Explain why an onion epidermis cell has no chloroplasts even though it is a plant cell, and why a plant cell nevertheless contains mitochondria.
questions.expected_answer: Chloroplasts occur only in green parts exposed to light; the onion bulb grows underground and is white, so its cells have no chloroplasts, although they have a wall and a large vacuole. Every living cell must release energy from glucose by respiration, so plant cells contain mitochondria and both photosynthesise (in green parts, in light) and respire (always).
